title: Premium Remittance Application Rules for Term Life Insurance
content:
**Premium accounting rules — Term Life Insurance.**

**Rule 1 (payable status).** A remittance is applied as premium only while the policy status is applied, in force or grace period. The status is read from the policy record of the policy the remittance is for.

**Rule 2 (retired).** The clause "a remittance is applied to the oldest billed installment that is still unpaid, one installment per payment record, and the paid-to date then moves forward by one premium-mode period" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Rule 3 (shortage).** A remittance short of the installment by no more than the product's premium shortage tolerance is applied as full payment, and the shortage stays on the outstanding premium. A remittance short by more than the tolerance is not applied and is returned to the payer.

**Rule 4 (retired).** The clause "money left unapplied after every billed installment is paid is held toward the next installment when it does not exceed the product's overpayment refund threshold, and is refunded to the payer as an overpayment when it exceeds it" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Rule 5 (lapsed policies).** Money received while the policy is lapsed is not premium: it is held with a reinstatement application and applied only on the reinstatement date, or refunded if no reinstatement follows.

| Policy status on record | Remittance applied as premium? |
|---|---|
| applied | yes |
| in force | yes |
| grace period | yes |
| lapsed | no — held with a reinstatement application, or refunded |

Hypothetical shortage cases against an installment of 210.00 under a tolerance of 2.00: a remittance of 208.00 is applied as full payment and 2.00 stays outstanding; a remittance of 207.50 is short by 2.50 and is returned.

superseded_clauses: A remittance is applied to the oldest billed installment that is still unpaid, one installment per payment record, and the paid-to date then moves forward by one premium-mode period.

Money left unapplied after every billed installment is paid is held toward the next installment when it does not exceed overpayment_refund_threshold, and is refunded to the payer as an overpayment when it exceeds it.
